subject: Regional cloud interruption — customer bridge & traffic handoff plan
messages:
From: Samir Patel <ops@acme-retail.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: support@acme-retail.com
Date: Sun, 28 Apr 2029 02:14:00 +0000
Subject: Partial outage — east-us and eu-west traffic failing

Hi Aisha,

We started seeing a cascade of 5xxs for our checkout traffic at ~01:50 UTC. The errors appear to be concentrated against the east-us and eu-west endpoints (region hints in logs below). Our traffic switched to retries and some customers reported latency spikes.

Can you confirm whether Redwood has a regional routing issue or if this is something on our side? We need immediate guidance: a short mitigation plan and whether we should initiate any DNS/edge changes.

I've attached a short snippet of request IDs and timestamps.

—Samir
Ops Lead, ACME Retail

Attachments: request-ids-snippet.txt (text)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <ops@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Apr 2029 02:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Partial outage — east-us and eu-west traffic failing

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads-up and the sample IDs. We're already on a bridge. High level: we've observed degraded routing at two cloud fabric peers affecting some west-coast and EU edge clusters; APAC is partially impacted with elevated latency for long-tail requests.

Immediate mitigation we can enact now (short checklist):
- Route-level fallback: we will flip ACME's traffic preference to our regional-fallback pool (lower capacity but healthy) in 5 minutes.
- Prefix KV cache warm-up: force warm-up for your most common prompt signatures to avoid cold-token amplification.
- Client SDK suggestion: pin to dedicated endpoint fallback (dedicated.redwood.com/acme) for critical checkout calls — avoids public routing.

Can you confirm an acceptable maintenance window for a DNS TTL bump from 60s -> 300s to reduce failover churn? Also share any internal rate limits we should be aware of. I'll loop in Karthik to coordinate the routing change and Vanessa on customer comms.

We'll update this thread and the status page.

Thanks,
Aisha
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Sun, Apr 28, 2029 at 02:14 AM Samir Patel <ops@acme-retail.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a cascade of 5xxs...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Apr 2029 02:33:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Partial outage — east-us and eu-west traffic failing

Aisha / team — on it. Engineering summary: a peering flap at cloud-provider-x caused an asymmetric path to our east-us and eu-west edge clusters. We've throttled the affected peering and are shifting traffic via our secondary fabric. Expected impact: 5–15% error rate during transition window for bursty requests; tail latency should stabilize within ~8 minutes.

Immediate actions I executed:
- Activated regional-fallback pool for ACME (effective now).
- Pinned routing for API tokens preferring dedicated pools where available.
- Started collection of verbose traces — pushed to S3 (edge-conn-trace-acme-logs.zip).

Recommended customer-facing guidance (for your email to ACME):
1) Short ask: Increase DNS TTL to 300 for the duration of the incident to reduce oscillation; we will revert after stabilization.
2) If you have traffic shaping for critical checkout calls, throttle retries to avoid amplifying load.
3) If you can route a percentage of requests to the dedicated endpoint (we can give a pre-signed token), that path will see much lower failure rates.

I'll stay on the bridge; will send a post-incident summary with timeline and root cause.

—Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <ops@acme-retail.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Apr 2029 03:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Regional cloud interruption — customer bridge & traffic handoff plan

Samir — short customer note I posted to the status page and mirror below. I've also created a shared incident doc with proposed customer-facing timeline and postmortem agenda (link copied in the related_links). Please review and flag any items:

Status update (public):
- We are investigating elevated error rates for requests originating in east-us and eu-west. Our mitigation includes routing affected traffic to a healthy fallback pool and enabling dedicated endpoints for critical calls. Customers may see brief latency changes while traffic shifts.

Customer-facing next steps (for ACME):
- Please increase your DNS TTL to 300 for the next 4 hours.
- If possible, route checkout calls to the dedicated endpoint we will provide.
- Send any additional request IDs or error samples to support@acme-retail.com; we'll attach them to the bridge.

I'll send a scheduled follow-up in 2 hours with stabilization status and a proposed postmortem slot.

—Vanessa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Regional cloud interruption — customer bridge & traffic handoff plan

Thanks all — update from our side: after moving 40% of checkout traffic to the dedicated endpoint and bumping TTL, error rates dropped to <0.5% and latency returned to baseline for most customers. We've kept rate-limiting tighter on retries and observed no downstream failures for payments.

Two asks before we close the bridge:
- Can Redwood share the initial bridge logs and the postmortem draft when available? We need the timeline for our internal compliance report.
- We would like to request a short follow-up call (30 minutes) this week to review RCA and confirm mitigation runbook changes.

Appreciate the fast support — Samir
